text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
LE MATIN DU SAHARA
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali tells Moroccan-Libyan commission "We can't hope for a better future unless it is within the framework of Arab Maghreb Union."
- Guinea Bissau withraws recognition of Saharan Arab Democratic Republic which is in conflict with Morocco over the Western Sahara.
- United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan meets his special envoy in Western Sahara James Baker on ways to speed up referendum proceedings.
L'OPINION
- Fuel stations workers and supply firms to meet in attempt to solve differences.
- Casablanca police dismantle prostitution network sending young girls to Gulf countries.
AL-BAYANE
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali in Libya to attend work of Morocco-Libya joint commission.
LE QUOTIDIEN
- Abdellatif Filali calls for lifting embargo on Libya. His visit shows extent of commitment towards Libya despite its isolation.
ALMAGHRIB
- Morocco and China sign cooperation accord for training and exchange of experience on public finance auditing.
- German Economy Minister Gunter Rexrodt expected in Morocco next week to inaugurate his country's chamber of commerce.
LA NOUVELLE TRIBUNE
- Stock Exchange index increased 40 percent in three months, the increase raises doubts about prices really reflecting value of firms.
L'ECONOMISTE
- Good company results are in line with forecasts but still do not justify big gains on the stock market.
($ = 9.2 dirhams)
